title: SCIM: quarantine-first deprovisioning and safe-retry orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our SCIM connector occasionally issues duplicate or conflicting deprovision requests to customer identity providers during transient failures (network blips, 429s, or IdP maintenance windows). This causes failed or partial deprovisions, orphaned accounts in Redwood, and confusing audit trails for customers relying on strict identity hygiene. Current behavior retries immediately and can cause ordering/race conditions when group removals and user deletions overlap.

Goals: 1) Make SCIM deprovisioning safe and reversible for a short window (quarantine-first) so accidental deletes can be recovered. 2) Ensure at-least-once delivery with deterministic deduplication so retries do not cause duplicated work or inconsistent state. 3) Add observability and admin controls so SRE/Support and customers can inspect and act on deprovision flows. 4) Keep changes gated behind a feature flag and rollout incrementally to connectors.

Design overview: - Quarantine-first flow: on receiving a successful delete request from an IdP or issuing a delete via SCIM, mark user/group as "quarantined" (soft-retired) for a configurable TTL (default 72h). During quarantine the account is inert (no active tokens, blocked SSH/API keys) but can be recovered with a reversible path. After TTL expiry a background reclamation job performs permanent deletion and emits a final audit event. - Idempotency+dedupe: require connectors to attach an idempotency_key formed from externalId|syncTimestamp|operation. Our SCIM gateway stores last-applied op per externalId and rejects exact-duplicate ops. For at-least-once scenarios we support op sequencing by maintaining a monotonic sync_token per connector and storing last-seen sequence for quick ordering checks. - Retry orchestration: implement exponential backoff with connector-specific rate limits and an in-flight-per-connector cap. Retries that fail due to 5xx or 429 will be scheduled into a connector-level retry queue; later retries check idempotency state before emitting. - Quarantine reconciliation: a periodic reconciliation job compares active IdP roster versus Redwood state to detect mismatches (orphaned users, missed deprovisions). Reconciliation can re-quarantine or queue remedial actions and annotates audit records with scim_event_id and reconciliation_run_id. - Admin controls: Console actions for org admins and Redwood SREs: "undo quarantine" (recover), "force purge now", and "resend to connector". Each action creates an immutable audit entry with actor, reason, and trace links. - Observability: emit metrics (scim.quarantine.created, scim.quarantine.recovered, scim.quarantine.purged, scim.retry.attempt, scim.retry.backoff_ms) and a dashboard with per-connector retry latency histogram and failure reasons. Provide a tracing span for each SCIM operation and include trace_id in audit events.

API/contract changes: - SCIM gateway will accept an optional idempotency_key header (X-SCIM-Idempotency-Key). If missing, gateway will synthesize a key but log increased risk. - New audit fields: scim_event_id, connector_sync_token, quarantine_ttl_seconds. - Connector config flags: quarantine_ttl_seconds, in_flight_limit, enable_quarantine (feature flag).

Acceptance criteria: - End-to-end test that simulates transient 503/429 on delete and validates user ends up quarantined, then recovered if IdP restores, or purged after TTL. - Unit tests for idempotency lookup and dedupe logic. - Load test showing per-connector in-flight limit prevents retry storms (no >N concurrent upstream requests). - Dashboard panels exist and alarms fire for retry rates > threshold. - Feature flagged rollout finished for 3 pilot customers without incidents.

Security & compliance notes: The quarantine state still respects retention/compliance policies; audit logs are immutable and exportable for SOC/Customer audits. KMS keys used to sign idempotency tokens are rotated per infra policy.

Rollout plan: 1) behind feature flag in gateway (canary 5% of connectors) 2) enable reconciliation in read-only mode to collect signals 3) enable write path for pilot orgs 4) expand to all connectors after 2 weeks of telemetry.

Links: - Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SO/SCIM+Quarantine+Design - Spike PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4091 - Dashboard (proto): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/SCIM/quarantine-retries

Notes on differences vs prior tickets: This ticket focuses on a reversible quarantine-first deprovisioning model + connector-level retry orchestration and admin tooling. It avoids permanent immediate deletes and emphasizes deterministic idempotency to prevent duplicate destructive operations.
